# Danske Multidisciplinære Psykiatrigrupper

Danske Multidisciplinære Psykiatrigrupper (DMPGer) are a set of Danish multidisciplinary psychiatry groups that appear in the corpus as the body responsible for developing clinical guidelines relevant to ADHD diagnosis and treatment in Denmark. According to the ADHD-databasen's 2023 annual report, "der er foregået et massivt arbejde i de Danske Multidisciplinære Psykiatrigrupper (DMPGer) ift. udvikling af retningslinjer bl.a. ift. udredning af ADHD på voksenområdet og på børne- og ungeområdet og både i hospitals- samt privat regi" [^src1] — meaning this work spans both adult and child/adolescent ADHD assessment, and covers both hospital and private-practice settings.

The group's work feeds directly into the operations of the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-databasen]], the Danish quality database that tracks treatment quality for ADHD patients across regions and departments [^src1] [^src2]. Several steering-group members sit across both DMPG and ADHD-databasen, a structural overlap intended to keep the two efforts aligned: "Flere styregruppemedlemmer er med på tværs af DMPG og ADHD-databasen, så vi får samstemt os" [^src1]. This shared membership is explicitly framed as a coordination mechanism between guideline development and quality measurement.

By the time of the 2024 annual report (covering the period 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025), DMPGer's guideline work had progressed to a specific, forthcoming product: a guideline on non-pharmacological treatment of ADHD. The report states that this guideline "vil give os mere viden, som vi vil anvende i arbejdet med at gøre denne indikator mere skarp og meningsfuld" [^src2] — meaning the ADHD-databasen intends to use the new guideline to sharpen and make more meaningful its quality indicator 5. This shows DMPGer functioning not as a static rule-maker but as an ongoing source of clinical knowledge that the quality-measurement system actively draws on to refine how it evaluates patient treatment.

Within the broader story of the corpus, DMPGer sits alongside the ADHD-databasen's own expansion — the database was widened to include data from adult psychiatry and private practices, and most of its quality indicators still fall well below the ≥90% standard, underscoring the vulnerability of this patient group and the need for better cross-regional and cross-municipal cooperation [^src1] [^src2]. DMPGer's guideline-development work is presented as one of the levers meant to help close that gap.
